title: audit current IN_STATES
headline: IN_STATES (normalize.py:230-242) is a 49-pair literal covering 37 distinct canonical values, expanded in place to 86 keys by the self-map loop at lines 252-254. Three structural defects confirmed, one hard and previously unrecorded: the key 'jammu & kashmir' is unreachable because the ck transform rewrites '&' to ' and ' before lookup. Otherwise the dictionary is sound: all 37 self-maps present, zero empty values, aliases internally consistent. SEPARATELY, and most importantly for the tasks that follow: the profile builder's tokenizer is NOT the pipeline's tokenizer (build_profile.py applies [a-z0-9]+ with no strip_accents, while normalize.py:317 strips accents first), so analysis_out/profile/ systematically mis-reports French address tokens -- 15 of 15 accented probes diverge, and the split is visible in the real data (fragment 'rignac' = 10,330 present, clean form 'perignac' ABSENT, France test_s1). The pipeline itself is accent-safe, so all five FR_REGIONS keys still resolve; the corruption is in the measurement instrument only.
source: _upstream/src/normalize.py lines 230-242 (definition), 250-254 (STATE_MAPS + self-map loop), 318 and 331-335 (consumption in normalize_address)
method: Parsed the dict literal with ast.literal_eval (no module import; polars is absent). Replayed the exact ck transform from normalize.py:331-332 over every key to test reachability. Scored all effective keys against addr_tokens['India'] in the six analysis_out/profile files using the per-key-minimum union bound, substituting the top-4000 cutoff for absent tokens.

self_map.note: The FR_REGIONS self-map omission alleged in AGENT_PROMPT.md line 28 does not apply to India.

defects.title: 'jammu & kashmir' key is unreachable
defects.evidence: normalize.py:331 does re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9& ]+',' ',c).replace('&',' and '). '&' is preserved by the character class then rewritten to the word 'and', so any component 'Jammu & Kashmir' yields ck == 'jammu and kashmir' and can only hit the sibling key. Replaying the transform over all 49 keys: 48 unchanged, this one is not.
defects.row_impact: unmeasurable - 'jammu and kashmir' is absent from top-4000 addr_tokens in all six files

defects.title: alias keys that are ordinary English words
defects.note: Token counts are UPPER BOUNDS on matching rows; the ck match is whole-component. 'in' has 2107/1897/4862 occurrences but is NOT a key in IN_STATES, so it is harmless; it is a US code and STATE_MAPS scoping isolates it.

defects.title: cross-dictionary canonical-code collisions IN_STATES vs US_STATES
defects.verdict: SAFE as written - separate dicts; normalize.py:318 selects exactly one via STATE_MAPS.get(country, {}). Live bug only if the maps are ever flattened.

defects.title: self-map loop leaks _m and _v into module namespace
the profile tokenizer is not the pipeline tokenizer (accent-blind)
defects.mechanism: build_profile.py:28 sets TOKEN_RE=re.compile(r'[a-z0-9]+') and applies it to bal=ba.lower() (build_profile.py:113,127) with NO strip_accents. normalize.py:316-317 calls strip_accents(s).lower() BEFORE tokenising. [a-z0-9] does not match e-acute/e-grave/a-grave/c-cedilla, so the profile splits an accented word at the accent while the pipeline keeps it whole.

real_profile_evidence.control_interpretation: unaccented French tokens ARE present at high counts, so the absences are the accent split, not top-4000 truncation

defects.relation_to_refuted_2: Orthogonal to, and explanatory of, the already-refuted FR_REGIONS finding. The pipeline strips accents before matching and FR_REGIONS keys are accent-free, which is exactly why France state resolution measured 100%.
defects.recommendation: Fix build_profile.py to strip accents before tokenising (mirror normalize.py:317 at build_profile.py:127). This is the ONLY change actually recommended, and it targets the analysis harness, NOT _upstream/.

defects.title: semicolon split divergence between profile and pipeline
defects.mechanism: build_profile.py:31 sets ADDR_SPLIT=re.compile(r'[,;]') which splits on comma AND semicolon. normalize.py:322 uses s.split(',') which splits on comma ONLY.
defects.reproduced: 'andhra pradesh; 500001' is two components in the profile (so the unigram 'andhra', 215298 total, is counted) but ONE component in the pipeline, giving ck='andhra pradesh 500001', which is NOT a key.
defects.consequence: a profile unigram count for a multi-word state name can overstate real matchability
defects.semicolon_prevalence: UNMEASURED - no semicolon field exists in the profile (has_comma records ',' only)
defects.recommendation: align the two splitters; low priority because prevalence is unmeasured

alias_groups.note: canonical values shared by >1 literal key; all internally consistent

data_reachability.cutoff_sum_caveat: A key whose every token is absent from the top-4000 list yields this meaningless 1979. NOT a frequency; deliberately not reported as one.

partially_absent_but_live.note: absent in 2-4 of 6 files but clear the floor overall

gaps: No row-level counts for the 36 keys below the floor: profile truncates addr_tokens at 4000/file; raw TSVs prohibited (<1 GB RAM).
False-positive rate of any key is unmeasurable from marginal token counts; ts/la/ch/ga are upper bounds, not measured misfires.
The cutoff sum bounds a key absent in all six files in total, but not how that mass distributes.
Whether 'jammu and kashmir' is intended to cover the ampersand spelling is a design question, not a data question.
Indic-script text is invisible to all unigram analysis: name_tokens and addr_tokens contain 0 non-ASCII tokens across all six files.
Per-row component structure: the profile stores unigrams per component, not component strings, so HOW a key matches cannot be confirmed, only that its unigrams occur.

recommendations.action: Fix build_profile.py to strip accents before tokenising (mirror normalize.py:317 at build_profile.py:127)
recommendations.effect: French addr_tokens become the tokens the pipeline actually emits

recommendations.action: Guard every France dictionary recommendation against defect 90: re-derive evidence with accent stripping first
recommendations.effect: prevents proposing entries for fragment tokens (ge, rignac, orl) the pipeline can never emit, while missing real tokens (evreux, nimes, defense) that it can

recommendations: Cite IN_STATES as 49 pairs / 37 canonical values / 86 effective keys, not '49 states'.
The self-map loop is correct for IN_STATES; do not carry the FR_REGIONS self-map defect over to India.
'jammu & kashmir' (line 239) is dead code; first item a follow-up task should look at.
36 of 86 keys are below the profile's measurement floor; claims about them need row-level access.
Do not treat the 5 India/US shared codes as a live bug; STATE_MAPS scoping isolates them.
recommendation_posture: Work order establishes ground truth and explicitly proposes no changes. Recommendations are recorded facts for follow-up tasks, not proposed edits.

explicit_key_reachability_clarification.note: Two grains are both correct; cite the one that matches your claim. The count of EXPLICIT (pre-loop) keys with a required unigram absent from all six addr_tokens lists is 26 of 49. The count of EFFECTIVE (post-loop) keys below the measurement floor is 36 of 86, because that figure also counts bare self-mapped codes (cg, jh, ml, py, ...).
explicit_key_reachability_clarification.caveat: a BOUND, not a measured zero: addr_tokens is truncated to top 4000 per file

citation_note: Cite IN_STATES as 49 pairs / 37 canonical values / 86 effective keys, not '49 states'.
